verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b, and the goal has support from two committers in the thread. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable design point: the frontend parse of output_plugin_libraries can stop the tool on a value the server accepts today. A committer who knows this code can settle that point, together with the backpatch question.

brief.title: pg_createsubscriber: check that output_plugin_libraries allows pgoutput
brief.problem: pg_createsubscriber always creates slots with pgoutput but does not check the publisher's output_plugin_libraries setting, added by commit 226e49cb. If a DBA removes pgoutput from that list, --dry-run succeeds and the real run fails at slot creation. The affected users run pg_createsubscriber against a publisher with a narrowed plugin list.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a check on the publisher that reads output_plugin_libraries from pg_settings once per database given with --database, because database and role settings can change the effective value. If pgoutput is missing, the tool fails early with an error and a hint. If the setting cannot be read (missing on an older minor, or no privilege), the check is skipped silently.
user_visible_surface: New pg_createsubscriber error: publisher does not allow the "pgoutput" output plugin in database, with a hint to add it to output_plugin_libraries.
New prerequisite in the pg_createsubscriber docs: the effective output_plugin_libraries for each source database connection must include pgoutput.
--dry-run now fails when pgoutput is not allowed in any target database.
Separate master-only doc patch adds a section "Installing Logical Decoding Output Plugins" to logicaldecoding.sgml.
author_claims: --dry-run passing while the real run fails is surprising to users.
The gap is an oversight in 226e49cb and could be backpatched to v17 and v18.
A per-database check is needed because ALTER DATABASE SET can change the value.
A separate patch frees the memory pg_strdup'd for max_slot_wal_keep_size.
brief.thread_state: Fujii Masao, Jacob Champion and João Rito favour master only and João Rito tested v7 and supports Ready for Committer; the author still questions the backpatch decision. The CF entry shows only the doc patch, so cfbot does not test the v7 code patch.
unclear: The thread has no agreed policy on what --dry-run should check, while other permission failures (REPLICATION, CREATE, publication ownership) still pass it.
The material does not say whether the skipped check should log anything, for example at debug level with -v.
The material does not include the v7 code patch prose, so the final message text and hint wording are not shown.
Jacob Champion plans to reject values like 'test_decoding, ' on the server, which would change the parse-failure path in this patch.
search_queries: logical replication slot creation permission check

objections.title: Client-side list parsing can reject settings the server accepts
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA sets output_plugin_libraries = 'pgoutput, test_decoding, ' on the publisher. The server accepts this value and pgoutput slots work. With the patch, pg_createsubscriber stops with a fatal parse error in --dry-run and in the real run, so a conversion that worked before now fails.
objections.argument: The patch re-parses a server GUC in the frontend with SplitGUCList, so the tool's view of the setting can differ from the server's. Message #29 shows that the trailing-comma value reaches the parse-failure branch. Message #31 calls the server behaviour a bug and plans a fix, but the material does not say whether that fix lands in the same release. The tool also turns a parse failure into a hard error, though the run would succeed today.
objections.author_must_show: Will the server-side fix that rejects empty list elements land before or with this patch, and if not, why should a parse failure stop the tool instead of skipping the check?

critic.reasoning: Message #29 confirms that a trailing-comma value set on the server reaches the pg_fatal branch, and v7 keeps that branch. Message #31 plans a server fix but gives no schedule, so the regression for such a setting is unanswered; the severity stays fixable.

committability.liability: The owner signs for a frontend copy of the server's list parsing in pg_createsubscriber.c, which must follow any later server change to that setting. The liability is small and stays inside one tool.

precedents_retrieved.title: pglogical_output - a general purpose logical decoding output plugin
precedents_retrieved.summary: Craig Ringer proposed pglogical_output as a contrib module for 9.6: a general-purpose logical decoding output plugin that streams changes in a documented binary or JSON protocol. It adds client-negotiated startup parameters, a relation metadata cache, and C and PL/pgSQL hooks for filtering rows and origins.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund's late review found design problems. He objected to the PL/pgSQL hooks, because output plugins may not access normal tables, and to having two output formats in one plugin. He also argued that the relation metadata cache is not safe against cache invalidations and that api_private leaks memory. Craig Ringer agreed to rework several of these points, but the SGML documentation was still unfinished, and Michael Paquier questioned whether the module belongs in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Considering that this module could have a happier life if managed independently.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_createsubscriber - more logging to say if there are no pubs to drop
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made pg_createsubscriber log "no publications found" when its step that drops all existing publications finds none to drop. The goal was to remove doubt about whether publications had been dropped silently.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed and then reverted. In --dry-run mode the publication create step does nothing, so the subscriber has no publications to fetch. pg_createsubscriber then logs "no publications found" and still logs "dropping publication", which made the output less clear. The author himself raised the problem and asked for the revert.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The bottom line is I think this patch can be reverted because it
didn't succeed to make things clearer, and may from some point-of-view
even make things less clear.

precedents_retrieved.title: This adds a new GUC parameter that automatically rolls back prepared transactions that have remained unresolved beyond the configured timeout. The cleanup is performed by the checkpointer process.
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrey Borodin, Artur Zakirov, Greg Sabino Mullane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, prepared_orphaned_transaction_timeout, that makes the checkpointer roll back prepared transactions older than the timeout. It is disabled by default (0) and is modelled on idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and similar timeouts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said a silent rollback breaks the 2PC protocol: after all participants PREPARE, COMMIT must succeed on a healthy database, and only the transaction manager knows whether a dangling prepared transaction should be committed or rolled back. An orphaned prepared transaction signals a serious malfunction that needs monitoring, and a DBA who wants a timeout can use a cron job. Users who enable 2PC are expected to have their own monitoring and handling.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Silent rollback in any scenario I can imagine is a disaster.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Trigger failsafe when VACUUM is run in single user mode
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a VACUUM option for single-user mode, first called VACUUM LIMIT and later VACUUM (EMERGENCY), that vacuums only tables whose xid or mxid age passes a fixed cutoff, with failsafe behavior and no index cleanup or truncation. The aim is to get out of single-user mode quickly after a wraparound shutdown.
precedents_retrieved.objection: During review, the thread found that the v14 failsafe already turns off heap truncation, so plain VACUUM should work under the postmaster at xidStopLimit. The plan then moved to removing the advice to use single-user mode. Noah Misch then showed that VACUUM can still create multixacts at multiStopLimit, so more work was needed. The author was away sick and withdrew the work for v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I gather from subsequent discussion that a full solution goes beyond just a new warning message and documentation. Either way I'm not quite prepared to address this in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical decoding to output generated columns
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Smith (smithpb2250), Shubham Khanna (skhanna), Shlok Kyal (shlokkyal)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let pgoutput send generated column values in logical replication, so consumers get a complete row instead of computing generated columns on the subscriber. The work added replication of generated columns named in a publication column list, then a publish_generated_columns publication parameter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Most of the work was committed before the entry closed: generated columns in column lists and the publish_generated_columns parameter. After that commit, Peter Eisentraut asked how the feature should work with the proposed virtual generated columns, which he thought could not be replicated, and Amit Kapila suggested limiting the option to stored generated columns. The thread then went idle in Waiting on Author, and Michael Paquier returned the entry until that question is settled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As of now this thread is just waiting on author and idle in the CF app for no real purpose.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix bug when calling strncmp in check_authmethod_valid
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the length argument of strncmp in initdb's check_authmethod_valid, which computes authmethod - strchr(authmethod, ' ') and so can be negative. Reversing the subtraction would make auth methods with options, such as --auth 'pam <servicename>', match the valid method list.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn. Daniel Gustafsson pointed out that the patched length is still wrong, because it compares against "pam" when it should compare against "pam ", so it needs a +1. He also noted that auth options have been broken for about 12 years and were never documented, and asked whether the code should be removed instead of fixed. No reply to that question is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: But, since it's been broken in all supported versions of postgres and has AFAICT never been documented to exist, should we fix it or just remove it?

precedents_retrieved.summary:

Reverted commit(s): Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2cf91ccb73ce888c44e3751548fb7c77e87335f2.

When using the old msvcrt.dll, MinGW would supply its own dummy version
of _configthreadlocale() that just returns -1 if you try to use it.  For
a time we tolerated that to shut the build farm up.  We would fall back
to code that was enough for the tests to pass, but it would surely have
risked crashing a real multithreaded program.

We don't need that kludge anymore, because we can count on ucrt.  We
expect the real _configthreadlocale() to be present, and the ECPG tests
will now fail if it isn't.  The workaround was dead code and it's time
to revert it.

(A later patch still under review proposes to remove this use of
_configthreadlocale() completely but we're unwinding this code in
steps.)

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier attempt at this idea. The thread cites no earlier discussion of it. Message #12 links a commit that let pg_createsubscriber reuse existing publications, and that commit is context only. No earlier rejection reason applies here.

Other compatibility points are settled in the thread. The patch is now master only, unreadable settings skip the check, and only users who removed pgoutput see new --dry-run failures, which their real run would hit anyway.

The proposal changes no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message or extension ABI. pg_createsubscriber only reads output_plugin_libraries from pg_settings over its existing publisher connections, and the guc_parameters.dat edit is a comment.

The check adds no privilege or exposure. It reads output_plugin_libraries through pg_settings, which returns a row only to roles that can already see the setting (superuser or pg_read_all_settings), and it prints the value only to the user who ran that query. Server permission rules and the pg_hba path are unchanged.

From the maintenance angle the cost is small and stays inside pg_createsubscriber. Users who never run the tool pay nothing, and the only runtime cost is one extra connection and query per --database. The client parses the setting the same way pg_upgrade/check.c already does, and a guc_parameters.dat comment records that dependency, so it follows existing practice. Two committers who know the area, Fujii Masao and Jacob Champion, are engaged (messages #17, #29, #31). Jacob Champion's reply in message #13 leaves open what --dry-run should check, but Fujii Masao answers it in message #17 with a workable rule: add the checks that are simple to perform. If the server later rejects values such as 'test_decoding, ' (message #31), the client parse-error branch could lose its purpose, but it would not fail and would not mislead users. Without the code, I could not check whether a value that names pgoutput with a path or with quoting is matched the same way on the client and on the server.

No existing feature, option or extension checks output_plugin_libraries for pg_createsubscriber before slot creation, and the check extends the existing check_publisher() path rather than adding a second mechanism. A manual SHOW in each source database is possible, but a committer would not treat that as a real alternative for a --dry-run check that two committers in the thread already support.

There are no field reports, and the failure needs a DBA to remove pgoutput from its default list (message #11), so the user group is small. The cost is small too and falls only on pg_createsubscriber users: one extra connection and query per database. Two committers support the check for master (messages #17, #29, #31), and a 'show demand' objection would not hold up against that.
